cues.say: Component 14: Replicas and failover. The primary database takes all writes. Replicas are live, read-only copies a fraction of a second behind. A standby takes over if the primary dies. You'll bring this up during the spike defenses.
Think of it as: A co-pilot ready to take the controls. Use it for more read capacity, and surviving a database crash.
Here's a real scenario. Heavy sales reports slow down checkout. Later, at 2 AM, the primary's machine fails.
Without it: Reports compete with checkout for the one database.
A hardware failure means hours of downtime.
With it: Reports read from a replica; checkout stays fast.
The cloud promotes the standby in 30 to 60 seconds.
Writes in that minute fail, and the app retries them.
Why it works: Replicas take read load off the one writer, and the standby turns a failure into a one-minute blip.
In the interview, say: Never read stock you're about to sell from a replica. It can be a moment behind.
A few related terms you may hear.
Failover: Promoting the standby when the primary dies.
Multi-AZ: Standby in another data center, same region. Always do it.
Multi-region: A full copy far away. Only if an hour down is unacceptable.
Point-in-time restore: Rewind to any minute, to undo a bad delete.
RPO: How much recent data you could lose.
RTO: How long you'd be down.
